description: Table 4 is a single rendered data table (no plots, no micrographs, no scale bars) reporting the mechanical properties of four tested low-density δ-ferrite steels, labelled R650, R750, R850 and R950. The five columns are headed: Specimen; IAE (J); UTS (Rm, MPa); TE (A, %); and SPP (Rm × A, GPa %). Every data cell is a mean with a ± standard deviation. R650 has the highest impact absorbed energy, 207.5 ± 29.3 J, with UTS 868.7 ± 16.4 MPa, total elongation 19.0 ± 3.2 % and SPP 16.5 ± 1.5 GPa %. R750 drops to IAE 75.9 ± 22.3 J and shows the lowest strength of the set, UTS 724.3 ± 7.0 MPa with TE 17.3 ± 3.6 % and SPP 12.5 ± 2.6 GPa %. R850 and R950 are strong but brittle: IAE falls to 5.6 ± 0.6 J and 4.6 ± 0.2 J while UTS rises to 1160.0 ± 15.4 MPa and 1254.5 ± 70.0 MPa, with TE 8.3 ± 0.1 % and 3.5 ± 0.8 % and SPP 9.6 ± 0.1 and 4.4 ± 1.0 GPa %. The table therefore documents the strength–toughness trade-off across the four rolling-temperature conditions: impact energy decreases monotonically with increasing strength, and the strength–ductility product peaks for R650.

observations.observation: The table has five columns headed 'Specimen', 'IAE (J)', 'UTS (Rm, MPa)', 'TE (A, %)' and 'SPP (Rm × A, GPa %)', so SPP is defined as the product of tensile strength and total elongation in units of GPa %.
Four specimens are tabulated: R650, R750, R850 and R950.
R650 records the highest impact absorbed energy, IAE = 207.5 ± 29.3 J, together with UTS = 868.7 ± 16.4 MPa, TE = 19.0 ± 3.2 % and SPP = 16.5 ± 1.5 GPa %.
R750 has the lowest ultimate tensile strength of the four, UTS = 724.3 ± 7.0 MPa, with IAE = 75.9 ± 22.3 J, TE = 17.3 ± 3.6 % and SPP = 12.5 ± 2.6 GPa %.
R950 has the highest strength in the table, UTS = 1254.5 ± 70.0 MPa, but the lowest impact energy and ductility, IAE = 4.6 ± 0.2 J and TE = 3.5 ± 0.8 %.

Impact absorbed energy falls monotonically with increasing specimen number, from 207.5 ± 29.3 J (R650) through 75.9 ± 22.3 J (R750) to 5.6 ± 0.6 J (R850) and 4.6 ± 0.2 J (R950); the steepest drop occurs between R750 and R850.
Total elongation decreases monotonically across the series: 19.0 ± 3.2 % (R650), 17.3 ± 3.6 % (R750), 8.3 ± 0.1 % (R850), 3.5 ± 0.8 % (R950).
The strength–ductility product SPP decreases monotonically from 16.5 ± 1.5 GPa % (R650) to 4.4 ± 1.0 GPa % (R950).
Every tabulated value is reported as a mean with a ± standard deviation, and the largest scatter is seen in IAE for R750 (± 22.3 J) and UTS for R950 (± 70.0 MPa).
The caption states that Table 4 presents the mechanical properties of the tested steels, which the table contents are consistent with.
